title: Biologists
description: Research or study basic principles of plant and animal life, such as origin, relationship, development, anatomy, and functions.

tasks.text: Research environmental effects of present and potential uses of land and water areas, determining methods of improving environmental conditions or such outputs as crop yields.
Identify, classify, and study structure, behavior, ecology, physiology, nutrition, culture, and distribution of plant and animal species.
Study basic principles of plant and animal life, such as origin, relationship, development, anatomy, and function.
Collect and analyze biological data about relationships among and between organisms and their environment.
Study aquatic plants and animals and environmental conditions affecting them, such as radioactivity or pollution.
Study and manage wild animal populations.
Study reactions of plants, animals, and marine species to parasites.
Program and use computers to store, process, and analyze data.
Review reports and proposals, such as those relating to land use classifications and recreational development, for accuracy, adequacy, or adherence to policies, regulations, or scientific standards.
Prepare plans for management of renewable resources.
Measure salinity, acidity, light, oxygen content, and other physical conditions of water to determine their relationship to aquatic life.
Develop pest management and control measures, and conduct risk assessments related to pest exclusion, using scientific methods.
Develop methods and apparatus for securing representative plant, animal, aquatic, or soil samples.
Plan and administer biological research programs for government, research firms, medical industries, or manufacturing firms.
Prepare technical and research reports, such as environmental impact reports, and communicate the results to individuals in industry, government, or the general public.
Write grant proposals to obtain funding for biological research.
Prepare requests for proposals or statements of work.
Represent employer in a technical capacity at conferences.
Supervise biological technicians and technologists and other scientists.

Develop and maintain liaisons and effective working relations with groups and individuals, agencies, and the public to encourage cooperative management strategies or to develop information and interpret findings.
Teach or supervise students and perform research at universities and colleges.
Communicate test results to state and federal representatives and general public.

skills.name: Science
skills.def: Using scientific rules and methods to solve problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Programming
skills.def: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C++, Oracle Java, Perl, Python.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Agilent Technologies GeneSpring GX, Basic Local Alignment Search Tool BLAST, BioKin PlateKi, BLAT.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Linux, UNIX.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Microsoft Access, Structured query language SQL.
